item.title: Erratum to Power boundedness and related properties for weighted composition operators on $\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, Journal of Functional Analysis 288 (2025), 110745
item.description: arXiv:2611.17382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As was kindly pointed out to us by S. Li, the proofs of Theorem 2.11 and Lemma 3.1 in our original paper contain errors that require modifications of the corresponding statements. We also correct a gap in the proof of Lemma 2.1, whose statement remains valid. Furthermore, we explain the consequences for several subsequent results and provide the necessary corrections to their statements and proofs.
item.dc:creator: Vicente Asensio, Enrique Jord\'a, Thomas Kalmes

item.title: Composition operators on weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.17392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a function $\varphi:\D\to \D$ holomorphic in a neighborhood of the closed unit disk $\overline{\D}$, we study the matrix \[ A_\varphi = \big(\widehat{\varphi^n}(k)\big)_{n,k\geq 0}. \] We obtain a complete characterization of those $\varphi$ for which $A_\varphi$ acts boundedly from $\ell^p$ to $\ell^q$, $p,q\in [1,\infty]$. These results can be reformulated in terms of composition operators, providing a complete description of the symbols $\varphi$ holomorphic in a neighbourhood of $\overline{\D}$ that induce a bounded composition operator $C_\varphi:f\mapsto f\circ \varphi$ between two possibly different Beurling--Sobolev spaces. In particular, we prove that $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\ell_a^p$ for some $p\neq 2$ if and only if it is bounded on every $\ell_a^p$, $p\in [1,\infty]$, if and only if $\varphi$ satisfies an analytic condition at the points of $\overline{\D}$ where it touches the unit circle. Extensions to weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces are also provided.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Charpentier (I2M), Rachid Zarouf (ADEF)

item.title: Noncommutative Rational Positivstellens\"atze with Operator Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.17493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a convex Positivstellensatz for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients. A hermitian operator-valued rational function that is positive semidefinite on a matrix convex set described by a linear pencil admits a positivity certificate consisting of rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term involving the defining linear pencil. The certificate comes with an explicit complexity bound independent of the dimension of the coefficient Hilbert space. As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional operator coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Abhay Jindal, Igor Klep, Jurij Vol\v{c}i\v{c}

item.title: The random KKM mapping principle and its applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.18408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on the recently developed random Brouwer fixed point theorem and the theory of stable compactness, we establish a random Knaster--Kuratowski--Mazurkiewicz (KKM) mapping principle in Hausdorff topological $L^0$-modules. As consequences of this principle, we obtain several results on fixed points, minimax problems, variational inequalities, and conditional games. These results solve a large class of noncompact problems in random functional analysis and its applications.
item.dc:creator: Tiexin Guo, Xiaohuan Mu, Qiang Tu

item.title: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $\Gamma$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
item.description: arXiv:2611.17543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $\Gamma$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $\Gamma$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $\beta_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $\beta_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Di Fratta, Valeriy V. Slastikov

item.title: A counterexample to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.17636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a unital \(\sigma\)-weakly closed subalgebra \(\mathfrak A\) of a von Neumann factor \(\mathcal M\) of type \(\mathrm{II}_1\), whose diagonal is \(\mathfrak D=\mathfrak A\cap\mathfrak A^*=\mathbb CI\). We show that there exist uncountably many faithful normal conditional expectations from \(\mathcal M\) onto \(\mathfrak D\) with respect to each of which \(\mathfrak A\) is a maximal subdiagonal algebra. Let \(\tau\) denote the unique normalized faithful normal trace on \(\mathcal M\). The conditional expectation associated with \(\tau\) preserves this trace, whereas none of the other conditional expectations is preserved by any nonzero finite trace on \(\mathcal M\). This gives a negative answer to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras in \emph{Amer. J. Math.} \textbf{89}(1967), 578--642.
item.dc:creator: Guoxing Ji

item.title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.17994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $\delta$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.
item.dc:creator: Jussi Behrndt, Badreddine Benhellal, Markus Holzmann, Konstantin Pankrashkin

item.title: Another step towards spectral descriptions of cyclic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the operator $V_f=M^{*}_{f}M_{f}$ in the weighted Hardy spaces $H^{2}_{\omega}$, with $M_f$ the operator of multiplication by the function $f$. We determine some basic properties like the essential spectrum when $f$ is a polynomial. Then we focus on the point spectrum when $f$ is a degree 2 polynomial and $H^{2}_{\omega}$ is the Bergman space, assuming that certain parameter is real. We show how this bifurcates into two possibilities: in one we establish the lack of eigenvalues while, in the other, the lack of maximal dimension eigenspaces.
item.dc:creator: J. Air\'an Santana-Rivero, Daniel Seco

item.title: Stochastic Nonlocal Conservation Laws with L\'evy Noise: Stability, BV Estimates, and Vanishing Viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2611.18051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study one-dimensional stochastic nonlocal conservation laws with a convolution-type interaction field, driven by multiplicative Brownian noise and compensated Poisson random measures. The nonlocal operator modifies the classical entropy structure, while the jump noise produces nonlinear correction terms in the entropy inequality. We introduce a notion of stochastic entropy solution and establish an $L^1$-stability estimate using spatial doubling of variables and the It\^o--L\'evy formula. This yields uniqueness in the vanishing-viscosity class and, under additional bounds, a localized Cauchy estimate of order $\sqrt{\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}$. Existence is obtained by vanishing viscosity: we construct the viscous solutions through a Faedo--Galerkin scheme and derive viscosity-uniform $L^1$ and localized $BV$ estimates, which allow us to pass to the limit and obtain a spatially $BV$ stochastic entropy solution.
item.dc:creator: Aekta Aggarwal, Debopriya Mukherjee, Akash Ashirbad Panda

item.title: Strong endpoint estimates for bilinear spherical averaging operators on closed hypersurfaces and curved patches
item.description: arXiv:2611.18061v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tainara Borges~\cite[Section~7.1, Question~7.2]{Borges2026} asked whether the strong $L^1\times L^1\to L^{1/2}$ estimate for bilinear spherical averages extends to all compact smooth hypersurfaces without boundary and with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We give a positive answer when $d\ge2$. The geometric argument concerns the difference projection $(y,z)\mapsto y-z$: at every critical point, two definite directions in its fiber already ensure that the projected surface measure has bounded density. This condition holds for the closed hypersurfaces in the original question. The ensuing strong endpoint uses the localization principle of Iosevich, Palsson and Sovine~\cite[Propositions~4.1--4.2]{IPS2022}. Our proof also establishes a partial positive result for the curvature-rank problem in Borges~\cite[Question~7.1]{Borges2026}. We exhibit a smooth full-curvature patch with boundary for which the strong estimate fails. The endpoint yields the entire fixed-scale H\"older family.
item.dc:creator: Xi Cen

item.title: Nuclear dimension of uniform Roe algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.18311v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for every discrete metric space $X$ of bounded geometry with Yu's Property A, the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ has nuclear dimension at most one. This answers in the negative a long-standing question of Winter and Zacharias on whether the nuclear dimension of $C^*_u(X)$ always equals the asymptotic dimension of $X$. Consequently, $dim_{nuc} C^*_u(X)\in\{0,1,\infty\}$ for every discrete metric space $X$, with or without bounded geometry.
item.dc:creator: Liang Guo, Kang Li, Jiawen Zhang, Jingming Zhu

item.title: Zong's problem on $2d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2609.38394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the intersection of $2d$ half-spaces containing the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{d}$. Equality in the radius bound characterizes the cube up to orthogonal transformations. The proof gives a lower bound for the average squared norm of the vertices, weighted by the Gaussian measures of their normal cones. This estimate follows from an inequality for the Gaussian measures of a simplicial cone and its projected facets, which in turn reduces to a linear estimate for the Gaussian centroid of a simplicial cone. We also discuss a quadratic extension of the problem and give a bound for it using an independent spectral argument. This bound implies that the intersection of any $m > d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{m}\,\ln\frac{m}{m-d}$.
item.dc:creator: Grigory Ivanov

item.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
item.description: arXiv:2611.01741v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0<\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ \lambda_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2\pi)^2\omega_n^{-2/n} |\Omega|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega) \frac{n}{n+2}(2\pi)^2\omega_n^{-2/n} |\Omega|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{\omega_{n-1}}{\omega_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove P\'{o}lya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Wang, Hehu Xie

item.title: Optimal MM* bounds for convex bodies
item.description: arXiv:2607.29458v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K\subset\R^n$ be a convex body in isotropic position. We prove the optimal mean-width estimate \[ M^*(K)\leq C\sqrt{n\log n}. \] The main new ingredient is a geometric inequality relating the Gaussian mean of the support function to its mean under the uniform measure on $K$, obtained through a heat-flow argument. Combined with the Gaussian-log-concave comparison of Eldan and Lehec and the newly available dimension-free bound on the third-moment parameter $\kappa_n$, this yields the result. The boundedness of $\kappa_n$ also makes the mean-norm estimate of Bizeul and Klartag sharp. Combining both estimates yields \[ M(K)M^*(K)\leq C\log n, \] extending Pisier's $MM^*$ estimate to non-symmetric convex bodies and to the isotropic position.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Bizeul

item.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.17712v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze resonance for partially dissipative systems, $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, where $A$ generates a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. {Resonance is} the phenomenon whereby a bounded, time-periodic $f$ yields an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, several other resonance notions, introduced here, may occur. Classically, {$T$-periodic solvability} is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-i\omega I)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces. The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.
item.dc:creator: Boris Muha, Sebastian Schwarzacher, Justin T. Webster

item.title: Nagata dimension, separation modulus and stochastic embeddings into trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.15672v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.
item.dc:creator: Ram\'on J. Aliaga, Rub\'en Medina
